notes: Statue Park is the largest open-air arena and the only one with almost no doors: two, across two hundred and twenty-eight pads. It is fought in the open between hard cover, which makes it the closest thing the game has to a field battle.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: There are essentially no doorways to fight at, so none of the threshold play that decides Bunker or Facility applies; engagements begin in the open at whatever range they are spotted.
nuance.because: The arena carries two Door records across two hundred and twenty-eight pads, the lowest door density of any stage.

nuance.claim: The statues and containers are the only hard cover, so movement is planned as hops between them rather than as routes along walls.
Because cover is freestanding rather than attached to walls, fights resolve by circling an object rather than by retreating from it, and whoever changes direction first usually wins.
Eight spawn points across a large open map means reappearances are far apart and hard to pressure, so map control beats spawn denial here.
nuance.because: The arena carries eight Spawn records, joint most of any stage, across two hundred and twenty-eight pads.

nuance.claim: Long open sightlines between cover make precision weapons genuinely effective, and a player holding the far end of an open stretch controls it.
There is ample distance to use explosives without self-damage, which makes those sets far stronger here than on any interior stage.
With no doorways and few forced paths, mines have very few reliable placements and are among the weakest sets on this stage.
nuance.because: Two Door records means there are almost no chokepoints to mine.

nuance.claim: The stage is dimly lit outdoors, so at the long ranges it fights at, a dark character is meaningfully harder to pick out against the terrain.
The two armours sit far apart on a large map, so going for one means crossing open ground and is a decision rather than a detour.
nuance.because: The standard two Armour records are spread across two hundred and twenty-eight pads.

nuance.claim: One-hit kills across open ground make crossing suicidal, so players hold cover and the match becomes a standoff broken only by flanking.
An unarmed carrier does better hugging the edges of the park than crossing the middle, since the open centre offers pursuers clear shots from every side.
